routes.label: Find and subtract the base angles

question: Triangles \(ABC\) and \(ADC\) are isosceles with \(AB = BC\) and \(AD = DC.\) Point \(D\) is inside \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle ABC = 40^\circ,\) and \(\angle ADC = 140^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle BAD?\)
solution:
Both isosceles triangles have base \(AC\), so their base angles at \(A\) can be found from their vertex angles. Since \(AB=BC\), the base angles of \(\triangle ABC\) are equal, giving
\[
\angle BAC=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ.
\]
Similarly, \(AD=DC\), so
\[
\angle DAC=\frac{180^\circ-140^\circ}{2}=20^\circ.
\]
Because \(D\) lies inside \(\triangle ABC\), ray \(AD\) lies inside \(\angle BAC\). Therefore
\[
\angle BAD=70^\circ-20^\circ=\boxed{50^\circ},
\]
which is choice D.
